title: Build a website with AI: destinations
objective: Build a one-page site with an AI build partner in one hour. Five shared levels teach the moves every builder needs; each of four destinations (Interactive elements, Style and design, Story and message, Under the hood) adds three levels of its own. Placeholder content: each checkpoint lists its planned steps.

project.description: A one-page site for something of yours: a club finder, a decision wheel, an event, a cause. Every level happens inside this project; there is no practice outside it.

build.title: Build with AI
build.description: Steering AI toward what you intend, and deciding what to do with what comes back.

language.title: Language of web dev
language.description: Naming the parts of a page and understanding how they work.

debug.title: Debug with AI
debug.description: Describing a problem so AI can help, and checking that the fix worked.

checkpoints.title: Welcome
checkpoints.description: Introduction, part 1 of 3. The student arrives, with an idea or without one.

panels.text: The moment in your project: The student arrives, with an idea or without one.
Introduced (info panel or video): What you will build today, what a destination is, and the one-hour plan. Short video and three panels.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Nothing yet. Continue to find your idea.

checkpoints.title: Find Your Idea
checkpoints.description: Introduction, part 2 of 3. You need a site idea you care about, and a destination to lean toward.

panels.text: The moment in your project: You need a site idea you care about, and a destination to lean toward.

Introduced (info panel or video): One question: do you already have an idea? With an idea: name it and describe it. Without one: a quick brainstorm with the AI, then name and describe it. Then pick a destination.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Answer the project name and description questions. The project is seeded from them.
Evidence the tutor sees: A project name, a one-line description and a chosen destination.

checkpoints.title: Your First Prompt
checkpoints.description: Introduction, part 3 of 3: the diagnostic. The project opens for the first time.

panels.text: The moment in your project: The project opens for the first time.
Introduced (info panel or video): A short skills check, then write your first prompt in your own words.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Write the first prompt and get the first version back.
Evidence the tutor sees: The first prompt, used to place the student on the map. Not graded.

checkpoints.title: L1 Steer It
checkpoints.description: Shared level, in every destination. The first version comes back and is a bit off.

panels.text: The moment in your project: The first version comes back and is a bit off.
Introduced (info panel or video): Two moves: add a detail (layout, colors, content or purpose), or change one thing and say what to keep the same.

In each destination: Interactive elements: Describe what the visitor does and what happens. Style and design: Describe colors, type and layout for one block. Story and message: Describe the tone and message of one section. Under the hood: Ask for one small piece of code and ask the AI to explain it.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Write a prompt with 2 or more details, or a follow-up that changes one thing.
Evidence the tutor sees: A prompt with 2+ specific details, or a follow-up that changes one thing.

checkpoints.title: L2 Use the Lingo
checkpoints.description: Shared level, in every destination. You point at part of your page in your own words and the AI changes the wrong thing.

panels.text: The moment in your project: You point at part of your page in your own words and the AI changes the wrong thing.
Introduced (info panel or video): Your page has blocks: the hero, feature cards, an interactive canvas and a call-to-action. Each one has a job.

In each destination: Interactive elements: Name the canvas and its controls, and say what each is for. Style and design: Name the hero, cards and button, and say what each is for. Story and message: Name the headline, card text and call-to-action, and say what each should say. Under the hood: Tell structure, style and behavior apart.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Name a block and say its job when you ask for a change.
Evidence the tutor sees: A prompt that names a block and its job.

checkpoints.title: L3 Keep or Redirect
checkpoints.description: Shared level, in every destination. The AI changes something and it only half fits your plan.

panels.text: The moment in your project: The AI changes something and it only half fits your plan.
Introduced (info panel or video): Compare it with your plan: what matches, what doesn't. Then keep it, redirect it with a new prompt, or edit it by hand when the change is small and exact.

In each destination: Interactive elements: Does it act the way you planned? Keep it, redirect it or edit it. Style and design: Does it look the way you planned? Keep it, redirect it or edit it. Story and message: Does it sound the way you planned? Keep it, redirect it or rewrite it yourself. Under the hood: Does the code do what you planned? Keep it, redirect it or edit the line yourself.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Say whether you keep, redirect or edit it, and why.
Evidence the tutor sees: A decision with a reason.

checkpoints.title: L4 Give Context
checkpoints.description: Shared level, in every destination. Something breaks or looks wrong.

panels.text: The moment in your project: Something breaks or looks wrong.
Introduced (info panel or video): Say what you expected, what happened and where.

In each destination: Interactive elements: Which click, what happened, what you expected. Style and design: Which block, what looks off, what you expected. Story and message: Which section, what reads wrong, what you expected. Under the hood: Which line or error, what happened, what you expected.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Report the problem with all three.
Evidence the tutor sees: All three in one message.

checkpoints.title: L5 Check the Fix
checkpoints.description: Shared level, in every destination. The AI offers a fix.

panels.text: The moment in your project: The AI offers a fix.
Introduced (info panel or video): Check that the problem is gone, then look for anything new that broke.

In each destination: Interactive elements: Click everything again to check nothing else broke. Style and design: Check phone size and the rest of the page. Story and message: Read the page top to bottom and check the flow still works. Under the hood: Check the fix and that nothing else broke.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Say how you checked.
Evidence the tutor sees: A stated check, such as "I reloaded and the image appears."

checkpoints.title: IA1 A list and a random pick
checkpoints.description: Own level: Interactive elements. You want the page to choose for the visitor.

panels.text: The moment in your project: You want the page to choose for the visitor.
Introduced (info panel or video): A list holds the options, a random pick chooses one, and the animation is just how it looks.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Describe the list and the random pick to the AI.
Evidence the tutor sees: Explains that the page picks one item from a list by chance.

checkpoints.title: IA2 A number and a rule
checkpoints.description: Own level: Interactive elements. You want the page to count, score or end a round.

panels.text: The moment in your project: You want the page to count, score or end a round.
Introduced (info panel or video): A number changes when something happens, and a rule says if this, then that.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Describe the number and the rule to the AI.
Evidence the tutor sees: Names the number that changes and the rule that uses it.

checkpoints.title: IA3 Remember and show
checkpoints.description: Own level: Interactive elements. You want a click to stay selected and to show a result right away.

panels.text: The moment in your project: You want a click to stay selected and to show a result right away.
Introduced (info panel or video): A list holds the choices, the page remembers what is picked, and a click can change what shows, such as a preview or a progress bar.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Describe what the page should remember and what should show.
Evidence the tutor sees: Names what is remembered and what changes on screen.

checkpoints.title: SD1 Layout and spacing
checkpoints.description: Own level: Style and design. The page feels crowded or unbalanced.

panels.text: The moment in your project: The page feels crowded or unbalanced.
Introduced (info panel or video): Space, alignment and order, described with block names.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Describe the layout change for a block.
Evidence the tutor sees: A prompt that names blocks and says how they should be arranged.

checkpoints.title: SD2 Style and consistency
checkpoints.description: Own level: Style and design. You change one block and the style starts to drift.

panels.text: The moment in your project: You change one block and the style starts to drift.
Introduced (info panel or video): Name the style in your own words and repeat it when you ask for changes.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Keep the style across two or more changes.
Evidence the tutor sees: A follow-up that restates the style while changing one thing.

checkpoints.title: SD3 Readable and clear
checkpoints.description: Own level: Style and design. Some text or a button is hard to read.

panels.text: The moment in your project: Some text or a button is hard to read.
Introduced (info panel or video): Size, contrast and wording make a block easier to read.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Ask for readability changes.
Evidence the tutor sees: A prompt that names a block and a readability change.

checkpoints.title: SM1 Say it in your voice
checkpoints.description: Own level: Story and message. You change one line and the tone drifts.

panels.text: The moment in your project: You change one line and the tone drifts.
Introduced (info panel or video): Name the tone in your own words and repeat it when you ask for changes.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Keep the tone across two or more changes.
Evidence the tutor sees: A follow-up that restates the tone while changing one thing.

checkpoints.title: SM2 Lead with the point
checkpoints.description: Own level: Story and message. A visitor could not tell what the site is for.

panels.text: The moment in your project: A visitor could not tell what the site is for.
Introduced (info panel or video): The headline and first line should say what the site is for.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Rewrite the headline and first line so they say it.
Evidence the tutor sees: A prompt or edit that states the site's purpose in the headline.

checkpoints.title: SM3 Make the ask clear
checkpoints.description: Own level: Story and message. The call-to-action is vague.

panels.text: The moment in your project: The call-to-action is vague.
Introduced (info panel or video): The call-to-action should say exactly what to do next.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Rewrite the call-to-action.
Evidence the tutor sees: A call-to-action with a clear verb and next step.

checkpoints.title: UH1 Read the console
checkpoints.description: Own level: Under the hood. Something breaks and the page shows nothing helpful.

panels.text: The moment in your project: Something breaks and the page shows nothing helpful.
Introduced (info panel or video): The browser console shows errors and where they come from.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Open the console and say what an error points to.
Evidence the tutor sees: Says which keyword or line the error points to.

checkpoints.title: UH2 Find it in the code
checkpoints.description: Own level: Under the hood. You want to edit one block by hand.

panels.text: The moment in your project: You want to edit one block by hand.
Introduced (info panel or video): Blocks have names in the code, and you can search for them.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Find the line or rule on your own.
Evidence the tutor sees: Points to the line or rule for a named block.

checkpoints.title: UH3 Undo to find the cause
checkpoints.description: Own level: Under the hood. Several changes have been made and something broke.

panels.text: The moment in your project: Several changes have been made and something broke.
Introduced (info panel or video): Undo one change at a time and check after each.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Find the cause and say how you found it.
Evidence the tutor sees: Names the change that caused the problem and how they found it.

checkpoints.title: Show it off
checkpoints.description: Finish. Shared by every destination. The build works well enough to share.

panels.text: The moment in your project: The build works well enough to share.
Used in your project (do it on your own): Share what you built.
